title: Accountability, easier to read
lede: The wrong leaderboard keeps its friendly poke, but the full ranking now reads like a first-class product surface: fewer competing concepts, an unmistakable return record, and receipts that open as complete incidents.

stats.n: Competing columns reduced to five labeled scan targets
Cramped table replaced by structured cards at 1024×900
Dedicated disclosure replaces the whole-row pseudo-button
Full red → continuous perceptual mix → full green

sections.heading: Desktop: a ranking you can parse in one pass
sections.note: Matched Creative Admin session, 2026–27 data, Volume ranking, 1440×1000 viewport, dark theme, and card top at y=150. Only the leaderboard presentation differs.

pairs.title: Full leaderboard summary
pairs.sub: The same nine people and 21 late events, before and after the hierarchy cleanup.
pairs.beforeCap: Eight columns compete with a five-item person subline; overdue, total, worst, and on-time figures carry nearly equal visual weight.
pairs.afterCap: Five scan targets group the diagnostics, make return rate prominent, and leave one clear control for the receipts.

sections.heading: Tablet: cards before compression becomes ambiguity
sections.note: Matched Creative Admin session, data, filters, 1024×900 viewport, dark theme, and leaderboard card top at y=551.

pairs.title: The open-sidebar breakpoint
pairs.sub: The viewport leaves 702px for the report surface.
pairs.beforeCap: The eight-column table exceeds its 702px scroller by 94px and wraps rows to 96px without making the labels easier to connect.
pairs.afterCap: Each person becomes a labeled three-signal card with a full-width history control and zero document overflow.

changes.h: Return record was easy to miss
changes.was: A small percentage shared the same weight as several adjacent time statistics, and sparse history appeared as an unexplained dash.
changes.now: The percentage is larger, carries its completed-return sample, and adds a rate-length bar whose fill is full red at 50% and below, continuously interpolates, and reaches full green at 100%. Sparse history says Not rated.

changes.h: The row mixed summaries with diagnostics
changes.was: Active overdue, total late, worst late, typical late, checkout count, on-time rate, and last incident were distributed across eight columns plus one crowded subline.
changes.now: Late events owns the active-overdue state; late-time pattern owns total, typical, and worst; return record owns percentage and completed returns.

changes.h: Every row acted like a button around real links
changes.was: The table row and mobile card were keyboard/click targets while also containing profile, checkout, and ADMIN action controls.
changes.now: Profile links and actions remain independent siblings, and one labeled 40px button owns expansion with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

changes.h: Receipts were split across table columns
changes.was: Booking title, due context, late duration, return state, and cleanup action were separated by the parent table grid.
changes.now: One incident-history region groups each booking and all of its evidence into a complete readable record.

changes.was: Dense evidence risked competing with the playful wrong-leaderboard framing.
changes.now: The stable shared jeers remain in the top-three spotlight; the full ranking stays calm, with the escape-route copy pointing people back to the return record.

verification: Focused contracts: 65 Accountability, jeer, route, service, RBAC, search, sidebar, and UI tests pass.

Static/build: TypeScript, focused ESLint, codemap/docs verification, whitespace check, and the 238-page build:app pass. The build ran from an isolated temporary copy so it could not disturb the shared dev server's .next directory.
Authenticated browser: The same nine-person board renders at 1440×1000 and 1024×900 with zero document overflow and no console warnings or errors.

Measured interaction: The desktop history button is 110×40px, exposes aria-expanded/aria-controls, and opens one 294px incident region containing four checkout links and four ADMIN action controls for the first person.
Color read-back: Live bars resolve to red/green mixes of 74/26 at 63%, 62/38 at 69%, 50/50 at 75%, and 36/64 at 82%; the source clamps 50% to all red and 100% to all green.
notes: Ranking order, filters, report API, CSV, custody evidence, permissions, and deterministic shared jeer selection are unchanged.
The top-three spotlight remains the playful layer; the full leaderboard favors accountability clarity over adding nine more jokes.

Authenticated visual proof and console read-back completed before the shared local dev process later exited; the managed sandbox denied the final port-bind attempt, so this static review is the durable handoff artifact.
No production deployment is part of this local UI slice.
